claims.text: The dynamic mechanical performance of HEAs results from heterogeneous lattice distortions that mediate dislocation dynamics.
Under dynamic loading, heterogeneous lattice distortions cause more uniform activation of multiple slip systems.
More uniform activation of multiple slip systems enhances strain-rate sensitivity.
Enhanced strain-rate sensitivity helps HEAs combine high strength with sustained ductility.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi can serve as a single-phase HEA with significant compositional disorder and local lattice distortions.
Compositional disorder in the HEA is associated with local lattice distortions.
Localized lattice distortions modulate dislocation mobility.
Compositional nanoclusters form and modulate dislocation mobility.
Heterogeneous distortions create local barriers and pathways for dislocation motion.
The local barriers and pathways permit dynamic activation of multiple slip systems.
Dynamic activation of multiple slip systems reduces dislocation pile-up.
The proposed dislocation mechanism delays work hardening.
The proposed mechanism sustains ductility while strength increases during fast deformation.
Relative to the conventional-alloy baseline, the HEA will show a steeper increase in dynamic yield strength with increasing strain rate.
Relative to the conventional-alloy baseline, the HEA will maintain greater ductility under dynamic loading.
At high strain rates, the HEA will exhibit more uniform slip-system activation than the baseline alloy.
At high strain rates, the HEA will exhibit a more spatially distributed dislocation structure than the baseline alloy.
The hypothesis is expected to apply to equiatomic or near-equiatomic HEAs at or near room temperature over strain rates of approximately 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1.
Microstructural variation and processing history may influence the dynamic mechanical behavior.
